original_question: For the maximum r-independent set problem on a continuous graph, does every yes-instance admit a polynomial-size certificate, equivalently a solution whose relevant point locations can be encoded with polynomially bounded rational data?
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, subsection "r-certificates" (an unnumbered open question): "Given any rational number r, is there a polynomial size certificate for the maximum r-independent set problem on general continuous graphs?" The needed notation comes from Section 2, Definitions 1–4, and Section 3.1, Definition 9. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right problem family (maximum r-independent set on continuous graphs) and the central issue in this part of the paper, namely whether optimal solutions admit polynomial-size certificates or encodings. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
missing_details: The paper quantifies over every fixed positive rational number r, not over arbitrary real r and not explicitly over a yes/no threshold k. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

The ambient object is a general continuous graph Γ built from a finite endpoint set and unit-length rectifiable continuous edges, equipped with the induced shortest-path metric d on all points of the edges. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
An r-independent set I⊆Γ is defined by the strict condition d(p,q)>2r for all distinct p,q∈I, and α_r(Γ) denotes the maximum cardinality of such a set. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
The nearby context frames the certificate question as arising when an α_r-preserving discretization of the edge set may fail to exist. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

The paper asks for a polynomial-size certificate for the maximum problem on arbitrary continuous graphs, rather than explicitly for "every yes-instance" of a decision problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

The claimed equivalence with "a solution whose relevant point locations can be encoded with polynomially bounded rational data" is not stated or proved in the paper; the only explicit nearby mechanism is an LP-based certificate for some small rational r, and the paper says that mechanism breaks down for larger r. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
refined_question: Fix a positive rational number r. Let Γ be a general continuous graph in the sense of Definitions 1–4: Γ has a finite endpoint set, each edge is a unit-length rectifiable continuous interval, and distances are measured by the induced shortest-path metric d. If I⊆Γ is r-independent when d(p,q)>2r for every distinct p,q∈I, and α_r(Γ) is the maximum size of such a set, does the maximum r-independent set problem on arbitrary continuous graphs admit a certificate of size polynomial in the input description of Γ that encodes and permits verification of an optimal r-independent set of size α_r(Γ)? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
justification: This rewrite matches the paper's exact open question in Section 3.1 and does not broaden it to neighboring questions about discretization, tractability, or approximation. It adds only the definitions the paper treats as prerequisite: what a continuous graph is (Section 2, Definitions 1–4), what r-independence means, and what α_r(Γ) denotes (Section 3.1, Definition 9). I did not keep the draft's "equivalently" clause, because the paper does not explicitly prove that polynomial-size certification is equivalent to polynomially bounded rational coordinate encoding; instead it only mentions an LP-based certificate for some small rational r and says that approach fails for larger r. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
